summary: a scientific task's tolerance by the person's standing rule: the reference's stated uncertainty, otherwise the larger of half a unit in its last printed digit and the run's own numerical error, a two-grid estimate of that error entering three times over; for a reference the source gives as exact, the run's own error alone

inputs.name: printed
inputs.meaning: the reference value as its source prints it, as text, its last digit kept as printed (a trailing zero included); in the quantity's unit; it may be null for a reference marked exact

inputs.name: stated_uncertainty
inputs.meaning: the uncertainty the source states for that value, in the quantity's unit, or null where it states none

inputs.name: run_numerical_error
inputs.meaning: the run's own numerical error of the quantity, in its unit, as an estimating skill gave it through the runner (the difference between two resolutions, or the standard error of a series the run produced); null where it was not estimated

inputs.name: run_error_from
inputs.meaning: how the run's own error was estimated: two_grids (two resolutions, as discretization_error_from_two_resolutions gives it), three_or_more_grids, or series_standard_error; null where the run's error is null

inputs.name: exact
inputs.meaning: true where the source gives the reference as exact (an analytic value of the case's own settings, a defined constant), so that it has no printed digit to be uncertain in and the half-digit branch does not apply; false or null otherwise

outputs.name: tolerance
outputs.meaning: the tolerance, in the quantity's unit; null, with why, where the inputs give none

outputs.name: from
outputs.meaning: stated_uncertainty, last_printed_digit or run_numerical_error: which of the rule's ways gave it; null where none did

outputs.name: run_error_estimated
outputs.meaning: true when a run's numerical error was handed and weighed, false when it was not estimated and the half-digit branch alone applied, null where the stated uncertainty was taken

outputs.name: factor
outputs.meaning: the factor the run's own error entered with: 3 for a two-grid estimate, 1 for three or more grids or a series' standard error; null where no run error was weighed

outputs.name: why
outputs.meaning: why no tolerance was given, or that the run's error was not estimated; else null

validity: one reference value of one quantity. The stated uncertainty, where there is one, is taken as handed: which uncertainty a source states (a standard error, the spread between its refinement levels) is the reader's to say. The last printed digit is read off the text as printed, so a trailing zero counts and a number already stored as a float has lost its printed form; an integer printed with trailing zeros is read as printed. A run's numerical error is taken as handed, with how it was estimated: estimating it is another skill's, and a run error handed without run_error_from gives no tolerance. A reference marked exact is taken as the source gives it: whether a value is exact is the reader's to say from the source, and an exact reference with no run error estimated gives no tolerance. It judges nothing, and a tolerance the person gave overrides it

source.citation: the person's standing rule of 2026-11-18 (docs/ideas/20261118.md, 'Tolerances by a standing rule', amended in 'Yes, run's own error' and 'Yes, factor 3'); JCGM 100:2008, Evaluation of measurement data - Guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement (GUM), BIPM (read 2026-11-18, https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/2071204/JCGM_100_2008_E.pdf; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261118-jcgm-100-2008-gum); NASA Glenn Research Center, NPARC Alliance CFD Verification and Validation, Examining Spatial (Grid) Convergence (read 2026-11-18, https://www.grc.nasa.gov/www/wind/valid/tutorial/spatconv.html; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261118-nasa-grc-spatial-convergence), after P. J. Roache
source.locus: GUM F.2.2.1, The resolution of a digital indication, printed page 64: half the unit of the last printed digit is the half-width the rule takes; NASA GRC, section Grid Convergence Index (GCI): the factor of safety is recommended to be 3.0 for comparisons of two grids and 1.25 for comparisons over three or more grids; the person's rule takes the first and keeps no factor for three or more grids

note: v3 with an input that marks a reference exact (the design role's reply f071852 to note 20261118-meta-macbook-20261118-1-4, item a; meta_agent/failures.jsonl rheotool-28-answered): an exact analytic reference has no printed-digit uncertainty, so the run's own error alone decides, entering with the same factors; without it no tolerance is given and the task stays undecided. Writing such a reference at a double's full precision, so that the half-digit branch gives nothing, is not needed and not the way. Every case of v3 gives the same with exact left out. Common, as v3 (every simulation bundle carries it; meta_agent/tasks/025). No value of a source stands behind the worked cases but the person's own example of 1066 K: each is worked by hand in its worked field.
